display.title: Episode 313: The Mountain of Ice (Tu B'Shvat)
display.summary_short: On Tu B'Shvat night, Uncle Yossi names the tzedakah-box contest winners, teaches what a tree teaches us, and tells how Rabbi Meir of Premishlan walked down icy steps without slipping.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the eve of Tu B'Shvat 5748. Uncle Yossi announces the winners of the tzedakah-box drawing contest, two sisters who made one picture together, and invites families to Tzivos Hashem's Jewish Children's Expo at the Javits Center in New York. After the Hakochainik march, two sisters from Beis Rivkah recite the Shema. Then a Tu B'Shvat teaching: tonight is the New Year for trees, when we eat fruits, especially the seven species of Eretz Yisroel, and say Shehecheyanu on a new fruit. A tree teaches that a person's fruits are good deeds, and its branches reach upward like hands raised in prayer. The story: in Premishlan, the mikvah stood on top of a steep hill whose steps froze in winter, and only Rabbi Meir walked them safely. Two visiting businessmen mock him, try the icy steps, and tumble to the bottom. When they come to apologize, the Rebbe explains: whoever is tied to the One above does not fall below. The show ends with Shabbos candle time.
display.lesson: When we tie ourselves to Hashem through Torah and mitzvos, we will not fall; like a tree, our real fruits are our good deeds.
